01.r: Every gift the Levites receive is to be drawn on.

02.r: What comes to the Levites from the people, chiefly the tithe.
02.n: Gesenius: a gift, a present, and also a gift offered to God. That 'your gifts' means what the Levites receive, and not what they own, is a reasonable reading of the passage, not something the word itself says. The DRC follows the Latin and rewrites the whole verse.

03.r: The Levites are to lift off a portion for the LORD.
03.n: The causative form of a verb that Gesenius and BDB give as to rise, be high: so 'make high, lift up'. It is the verb from which 'contribution' later in the verse is formed. The 'you' is plural: the Levites.

04.r: Marks 'all the contribution of the LORD' as the object of 'lift up'.
04.n: This small word marks a definite direct object and has no English equivalent; it is counted here with 'all'.

05.r: The whole of what is due to the LORD, none held back.
05.n: BDB notes that with a following noun this word means 'the whole of'. Because 'the contribution of the LORD' is definite, 'all the' or 'the whole' fits better than the KJV's 'every'; YLT says 'the whole'.

06.r: The portion lifted off and set apart for the LORD.
06.n: Gesenius derives the noun from the verb 'lift up' and gives an oblation, offering, gift, especially brought to the temple and the priests. We keep 'contribution' throughout, where older translations say 'heave offering'.

07.r: The personal name of Israel's God.
07.n: Gesenius records the phrase 'contribution of the LORD' as a fuller name for this offering.

08.r: The portion is to be drawn from the whole.

09.r: The finest of the gifts, not the leftovers.
09.n: Literally 'its fat'. Gesenius gives fat, and figuratively the best or most excellent of any kind, as in 'the fat of the land'. Geneva and YLT keep 'fat'.

10.r: Marks 'its holy part' as a further object of 'lift up'.
10.n: This small word marks a definite direct object and has no English equivalent; it is counted here with 'its holy part'.

11.r: The part of the gift that belongs to God and is set apart for him.
11.n: This word usually means a sanctuary. Gesenius cites this very verse for an earlier sense, a holy thing, something consecrated, and notes that the form here is unusual. 'Its best' and 'its holy part' describe the same portion.

_extra.8: ἢ (or): nothing in the Hebrew answers to it.

03.n: Dictionary form supplied by hand: the brief gives none. ἀφελεῖτε, 'you shall take off'.

06.n: ἀφαίρεμα, 'something taken off', from the same Greek verb as 'take off' before it, much as the Hebrew noun comes from its verb. The Greek has no word for 'all'.

09.n: ἀπαρχή, 'firstfruits, first portion', where the Hebrew says 'its fat', its best.

11.n: Dictionary form supplied by hand: the brief gives none. τὸ ἡγιασμένον, 'the thing made holy'.
